findings.title: Slots inside a date override bypass the busy-time check
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable, when a slot's date matches a date override and the slot is inside the override window, the function returns true immediately. It never reaches the busy.every(...) check against existing Cal bookings and connected-calendar busy times. A fixed or round-robin host who has a date override on a day can therefore be shown as available at times when they already have a booking or calendar event, allowing double-bookings on override days.

findings.title: Only the first same-day date override is considered
findings.body: The dateOverrides.find(...) callback returns true as soon as the slot falls outside the first override that shares the slot's date. If a user has two override ranges on the same day (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-17:00, which Cal.com allows as separate availability rows), a slot inside the second range is judged against the first range, find() stops, and checkIfIsAvailable returns false. Valid slots in the second and later override ranges of the day are incorrectly removed, notably for fixed hosts in round-robin events.

findings.title: Override containment check admits partially overlapping slots
findings.body: A slot is treated as inside a date override unless its end is at/before the override start or its start is strictly after the override end. A slot that starts before the override begins but ends inside it (e.g. 13:30-14:30 for a 14:00-18:00 override) is not flagged as outside and is reported available, and a slot starting exactly at the override end is also treated as inside because isAfter is used instead of isSameOrAfter. Bookings can therefore start before the host's override availability begins or exactly when it ends.

findings.title: Empty date-override detection compares Dayjs objects with ===
findings.body: The condition dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes') === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, 'minutes') compares two distinct Dayjs object references, so it is always false and the intended zero-length override case never triggers. For an 'unavailable' date override where start equals end, a slot straddling that instant satisfies neither the before-start nor after-end branch, so the function falls through to returning true and offers a slot on a day the host marked unavailable.

findings.title: Working-hours gate is wrong for split schedules and days off
findings.body: The workingHours.find(...) check returns 'outside working hours' if ANY working-hour entry for that weekday does not cover the slot, so a host with split hours (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00 on the same day) has afternoon slots rejected because the morning entry does not cover them. Conversely, if no entry lists the slot's weekday at all, find() returns nothing and the check passes entirely, so a fixed host can still be booked on a day off whenever a round-robin host's availability generated that slot. Both cases defeat the fixed-host enforcement this block was added for.

findings.title: Working-hours end check uses the slot start instead of the slot end
findings.body: Both start and end are computed as slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute(), so the end > workingHour.endTime comparison never looks at when the proposed booking actually finishes. A 60-minute slot starting at 16:30 in a 09:00-17:00 schedule passes the check even though it ends at 17:30, letting fixed hosts be booked beyond the end of their working hours.

findings.title: Timezone-shifted override can be assigned to the wrong invitee day
findings.body: The new code converts the override wall time by the invitee-minus-organizer offset and keeps only hour/minute, discarding the resulting date, while the activeOverrides filter above still selects overrides by comparing the unshifted UTC-encoded start against the invitee day. For an organizer ahead of the invitee (e.g. a 09:00 override in UTC+10 viewed from UTC), the converted time is 23:00 on the previous invitee day, but the filter attaches it to the following invitee day, so the slot is offered a day late instead of on the correct day.

findings.title: No test covers the fixed-host round-robin override scenario
findings.body: The PR description states the main fix is that date overrides of fixed hosts restrict round-robin events, but the only added test re-queries a personal (non-team) event in Asia/Dhaka versus Asia/Kolkata and expects identical UTC slots. Nothing exercises a ROUND_ROBIN event type with an isFixed host who has a date override, the new checkIfIsAvailable override/working-hours paths for fixed and loose hosts, or a timezone change that crosses a date boundary, so regressions in the primary claimed behavior would go undetected.
